summary: The Organization of MISO States moves for acceptance of late comments and conditionally supports MISO's Zero Injection Generator Interconnection Agreement, asking FERC to require reliability, cost-shifting, resource adequacy and transparency safeguards.
ask: Accept the late comments, and approve MISO's ZGIA only if reliability, cost, resource adequacy and transparency protections are clear and enforceable, while treating it as one part of a broader large-load framework.

points.point: OMS offers conditional support for the ZGIA and does not oppose it.
points.quote: OMS cautiously supports the ZGIA proposal

points.point: OMS treats the ban on injection beyond the substation as a reliability requirement and wants studies before execution.
points.quote: That limitation must be treated as a reliability requirement, not merely a contractual condition.

points.point: OMS objects that MISO left the Transient Tolerance Window definition to its Business Practice Manual.
points.quote: MISO has deferred establishing an explicit definition of the appropriate Transient Tolerance Window to the development of its Business Practice Manual.

points.point: OMS backs keeping the ZGIA limited to generation and load at one substation and voltage level.
points.quote: recommends that the Commission accept the common-substation and voltage-level limitation as the appropriate scope of ZGIA.

points.point: OMS supports the requirement that the generator's full output serve the associated load for at least five years.
points.quote: with an expected period of at least five years.

points.point: OMS says upgrades needed if supporting generation fails to materialize should not automatically fall on existing customers.
points.quote: the costs of that incremental need should not automatically shift to existing transmission customers.

points.point: OMS asks MISO to explain ZGIA treatment across its resource adequacy models, including LOLE, UCAP, SAC and the Planning Resource Auction.
points.quote: OMS requests that MISO explain in a compliance filing, subsequent BPM rules, or a workshop how ZGIA resources and associated loads will be represented in

points.point: OMS wants any later move to injection rights sequenced so it does not bypass the Definitive Planning Process queue.
points.quote: must not allow a ZGIA resource to circumvent or obtain an advantage over interconnection customers already participating in the DPP queue.

points.point: OMS asks FERC to judge the ZGIA together with MISO's other large-load reforms on a complete record.
points.quote: the Commission should evaluate the ZGIA Filing together with other reforms developed during that process only after a complete record is developed

throughLine.text: State regulators comment on MISO's ZGIA filing in ER26-3552, MISO's first response to the E-8 order on co-located load, and ask FERC to weigh it with the rest of the E-8 response.

figures.quote: shall be no greater than 20 seconds
